commits.message:
feat(security): add versioned resolution of incident holds

- Add securityHoldVersion to the User model through an additive migration
- Increment the version on every new security incident
- Reject stale resolutions with version checks
- Add an OWNER-only endpoint to resolve holds
- Prevent suspending accounts with an active security hold
- Add unit and integration tests with SQLite
- Document the incident protection and resolution flow

commits.oldHeader: feat(seguridad): añadir recuperación obligatoria tras un incidente (E2)
commits.message:
feat(security): require account recovery after an incident (E2)

- Schema and migrations: mandatory recovery fields (passwordResetRequiredAt,
  securityRecoveryEmail, notifiedEmail), tokens with a SELF_SERVICE or
  SECURITY_RECOVERY purpose bound to a destination and version, and an
  optional actorUserId in AdminAuditLog (20261102090000 and 20261103120000).
- An incident report proposes the notified email as the destination; while
  recovery is pending, login (423) and sessions are blocked.
- When an OWNER lifts the protection, mandatory recovery starts and the link
  is sent to the authorized destination; the OWNER can correct the
  destination or resend the link.
- Link consumption (POST /api/auth/security-recovery/complete) and the
  /recuperar-cuenta page.
- Public request for a new link (POST /api/auth/security-recovery/request):
  always sent to the stored destination, generic response, per-IP limit and
  per-account cooldown; delivery in the background with graceful shutdown.
- New actions are audited without destination, token or link; the public
  request is recorded without an actor and the panel shows it as an
  unauthenticated request.
- Unit and integration tests with SQLite and documentation in docs/seguridad.

Pending: web page to request the link and panel labels (E4).

commits.oldHeader: feat(web): recuperación desde el login, auditoría, diálogos accesibles y panel admin móvil (E4, F1a, M1)
commits.message:
feat(web): add recovery from login, audit labels, accessible dialogs and a mobile admin panel

E4 - Mandatory recovery (web and documentation)
- New public page /recuperar-cuenta/solicitar to request a new recovery
  link, linked from the login (423) and from a closed link.
- Audit: centralized labels for the 8 actions, origin of the recovery
  destination and a filter for the new actions.
- Documentation of incident protection and mandatory recovery.

F1a - Accessible dialogs in the administration panel
- useModalDialog hook: initial focus, native Tab confined at the edges,
  Escape according to canClose and focus restoration; pure logic in
  dialogFocus.
- Scrolling that honours prefers-reduced-motion and an aria-label on the
  remove filter button.

M1 - Administration panel on mobile (< 768 px; desktop unchanged)
- No duplicated padding, summary in two columns and details in one.
- Users and audit entries as cards with touch actions; action availability
  moves to userActionsAvailability, shared with the table.

Tests: web 155/155, typecheck, oxlint and build pass.

commits.oldHeader: feat(auth): add email verification and background recovery delivery
commits.message:
feat(auth): add email verification and background recovery delivery

Consolidates the Fase 0 work that was pending in the working tree before
the PostgreSQL integration:

- Email verification: single-use tokens, date-based policy with a grace
  period, verification page, resend form and session notices.
- Self-service password reset issued and delivered in the background,
  with the same generic response for every account.
- Hardened email change and mandatory security recovery flows, with
  route and service tests.
- SQLite migration for email verification.
- Security documentation for email verification and the Fase 0
  deployment checklist.

commits.oldHeader: feat: add publication checklist, property status and request lifecycle hardening
commits.message:
feat: add publication checklist, property status and request lifecycle hardening

Publication checklist:
- Manual checklist for Idealista, Fotocasa, Pisos.com, Yaencontre and
  Habitaclia with local logos, a link to each portal home page and a
  link to the listing only when it is marked with a valid URL.
- Up to five custom "Otro/a" rows with name and home page, at least
  one always present.
- Centralised URL validation shared by web and API, server-side
  ownership checks and integrity constraints.
- No automatic publishing from EstateForge.

Property status:
- Commercial status (for sale, sold, for rent, rented) kept separate
  from the physical condition; older properties without a status keep
  working.

Validation and generation:
- Numeric listing validator accepts thousands separators, decimals,
  signs and negative floors while still flagging real inconsistencies.
- Controlled responses for AI provider errors.

Request lifecycle and security:
- Request work tracking, graceful shutdown that waits for in-flight
  work and background deliveries, idle connection handling.
- Closed-field logging that never writes recipients, tokens or SQL.
- Single lock order for account rows.
- Logout warns about unsaved checklist changes.

commits.oldHeader: feat: migrate persistence from SQLite to PostgreSQL
commits.message:
feat: migrate persistence from SQLite to PostgreSQL

- PostgreSQL 17 through Prisma 7.9.1 and @prisma/adapter-pg; the
  libsql adapter is removed and DATABASE_URL must be postgresql://,
  with no silent fallback to SQLite.
- Single baseline migration (0_postgresql_baseline) with CHECK
  constraints and the partial unique index of the checklist; the SQLite
  migration history is archived unchanged in prisma/sqlite-history.
- Exact prices as Decimal(12,2), lowercase email identity enforced in
  the database, timestamptz dates.
- Configurable connection pool, PORT and HOST, connection
  application_name and /health/ready readiness check.
- Row locks for concurrent recovery (PG-20, PG-21) and checklist saves.
- Repeatable localhost-only development seed.
- Integration tests against a real local PostgreSQL server and
  operational documentation (migrations, backup and restore, recovery).

commits.oldHeader: fix: return 503 when PostgreSQL is unavailable and revoke undelivered recovery links
commits.message:
fix: return 503 when PostgreSQL is unavailable and revoke undelivered recovery links

Database availability:
- Central classification of availability errors (pool timeout,
  connection limit, unreachable or restarting server, closed pool).
- These now answer 503 with Retry-After and a generic body; integrity,
  validation and programming errors keep their 4xx or 500 responses.
- Only closed fields are logged.

Connection pool:
- The application owns the pg pool and closes it at the end of the
  graceful shutdown, after pending work and deliveries.
- Queries after the pool is closed fail instead of reconnecting.

Password recovery:
- When delivery of a reset or recovery link is known to have failed,
  only that unused token is revoked, so no useless active link is left
  and the recovery cooldown is released.
- An unconfirmed delivery keeps its token.
- Bounded SMTP timeouts.

commits.oldHeader: fix(api): answer 503 for checklist pool saturation and make the dev seed reusable
commits.message:
fix(api): answer 503 for checklist pool saturation and make the dev seed reusable

- The checklist save treated P2028 "Unable to start a transaction in the
  given time" as a write conflict (409). Availability errors now reach
  the global handler (503); a transaction expired while waiting for a
  lock is still a conflict.
- The development seed closed only the Prisma client, so with the
  application-owned pool the process stayed alive. It now closes the
  pool, runs in one transaction per account, is idempotent and creates
  representative data: two accounts, the four commercial statuses, a
  property without status and a checklist with "Otro/a" rows.
- The seed is now type-checked and covered by integration tests,
  including running it as a script.

commits.oldHeader: test(api): cover startup without database configuration and fix shutdown test timing
commits.message:
test(api): cover startup without database configuration and fix shutdown test timing

- New startup test runs the real server from an empty directory, so
  dotenv cannot load a developer .env. It checks that a missing, empty,
  SQLite or MySQL DATABASE_URL and an invalid PORT exit with code 1 for
  that reason, without printing the URL.
- The shutdown test for idle versus active connections waited 1 s for
  the exit. The shutdown contract places it at the end of the total
  timeout. It only passed on Windows because idle sockets are reported
  closed later there; measured behaviour is identical on Windows and
  Linux.

commits.oldHeader: chore(dev): add WSL PostgreSQL setup scripts and document the development database
commits.message:
chore(dev): add WSL PostgreSQL setup scripts and document the development database

- scripts/wsl/instalar-herramientas.sh installs Node.js 24.19.0,
  pnpm 11.20.0 and PostgreSQL 17 from PGDG in user space without sudo.
  It verifies the Node GPG signature, the PGDG key fingerprint and the
  signed index, and the SHA-256 of every package.
- scripts/wsl/postgres-dev.sh init/start/stop/status sets up a local-only
  cluster on 127.0.0.1:55432. It uses an unprivileged application role
  that owns the development and shadow databases and a separate test
  role; random credentials stay outside the repository.
- Optional SHADOW_DATABASE_URL so migrate dev does not need CREATEDB.
- New .env.example entries for the shadow database, connection name,
  PORT and HOST.
- .gitattributes keeps shell scripts in LF.
- PostgreSQL development, testing and graceful shutdown documentation,
  including the Linux SIGTERM results.
